names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 21 martie, «Sfântul Ierarh Toma, Patriarhul Constantinopolului».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 21 Μαρτίου, «Άγιος Θωμάς Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινούπολης», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's third heading for the Julian 21 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Свети Тома патријарх цариградски.“, with Свети left off, which is not a rank, and with the see патријарх цариградски left off as well. The heading gives no epithet, so the bare forename is what the source gives.

death.note: saint.gr: «Κοιμήθηκε ειρηνικά στις 20 Μαρτίου του 610 μ.Χ. και κηδεύτηκε στις 22 του ιδίου μηνός» — he fell asleep on 20 March 610 and was buried on the 22nd of the same month. doxologia.ro gave only the reign of Phocas, «(602-610)», which is the interval the corpus first held; the Greek page states the year, and it falls inside that reign.

source.text: doxologia.ro, calendarul zilei pentru 21 martie — «Sfântul Ierarh Toma, Patriarhul Constantinopolului»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 21ης Μαρτίου — «Άγιος Θωμάς Πατριάρχης Κωνσταντινούπολης»

attestations.note: «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 21 Μαρτίου εκάστου έτους.» This is the entry on which saint.gr itself says the day is unsettled: «Αρχαιότερα χειρόγραφα ορίζουν την μνήμη του στις 18 και 22 Φεβρουαρίου και στις 19, 20, 22 Μαρτίου» — older manuscripts put his memory on 18 and 22 February and on 19, 20 and 22 March — and it adds that the Paris Codex 1587 and the Petersburg Codex 227, at 19 and 20 March, also carry the feast of the translation of his relics. The row records the day page that listed him, which is 21 Μαρτίου, and the manuscript days are noted here rather than moved into rows of their own. The page also says «Η Σύναξη αυτού ετελείτο στην Μεγάλη Εκκλησία», his synaxis used to be held at the Great Church.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 03.04.2026 (21. март ст. ст.) — „Свети Тома патријарх цариградски.“

attestations.note: The day's third entry, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek already keep in this folder, and the same patriarch: raised to be sakellarios of the Patriarchate by John the Faster, chosen patriarch after Cyriacus, and dead in 610 — the same year this folder already holds, so no date was touched. It is set in the reigns of Maurice and Phocas. The entry carries the sign of the crosses that swayed and struck one another of themselves in a procession, and Theodore of Sykeon's reading of it: that it foretold great troubles for the Church and for the Greek empire from quarrels of religion and of politics, in which Christians would beat and destroy one another. Both men this folder already keeps are `related` to it already, and no row was added. Cyriacus, the predecessor the entry names, was not read as any folder in this corpus and takes nothing. The stored form is the bare forename, because Свети is not a rank and патријарх цариградски is the see this folder keeps in `office`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
